title: FAQs — Flat and Jump racing
note: BHA operational guidance consistently distinguishes Flat races from Jump races, including starting, racecourse and licensing contexts; sufficient to verify the two code-level Concepts without claiming one jurisdiction defines the entire global sport.

title: About IFHA
note: IFHA identifies itself as the global leader for the international sport of thoroughbred racing and promotes worldwide thoroughbred racing and breeding.

title: What Is Harness Racing?
note: USTA describes Standardbreds pulling a two-wheeled racebike steered by a driver; use as North American authority evidence for the core harness-racing Concept.

title: The Racetrack Experience — Pacers vs. Trotters
note: USTA states harness races are divided into pacing and trotting gaits and explains same-side versus diagonal-leg movement.

title: What is Banei Tokachi?
note: Official guide defines Banei as large draft horses racing on a 200m straight course while pulling a weighted iron sled over obstacles.

title: International Agreement — comparative metric/imperial race distances
note: IFHA publishes metric/imperial race-distance equivalences and race-distance measurement guidance; supports the core units and race-distance Concept.

title: 競馬用語辞典 — 着差
note: JRA defines race margins using ハナ, アタマ, クビ and 馬身 and explains the nose-point basis of finishing margins.

title: Handicapping tools — Sectional timing
note: BHA explains that a race can be broken into sections, usually furlong by furlong, and that sectional times describe those portions of a race.

title: レース結果の見方
note: JRA result guidance explicitly labels 200m segment times as 区間タイム and explains finish-back 4F/3F timing.
